subject: Skip a tour stop that has nothing to show yet, instead of ending the tour there
body:
Step 4 opens a paid run, and a deployment with no paid run has none to
open. Next was disabled there, which is right about step 4 and wrong about
everything after it: the foundry and the status page always exist, and a
reader could not reach them until somebody had been paid.

Next and Back now move to the nearest step whose subject exists, and the
panel says which step it passes over and why. A step with nothing to show
is still never a destination. The README no longer says /archive shows the
Blitz contract; /contracts lists it under Superseded, and /archive holds
stored runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Let the issuer reclaim a dividend nobody can hold, and redeploy CorpusShares
body:
A dividend declared while no share exists is owed to nobody: at its record
date every holder's entitlement is zero, so no claim can ever succeed. The
first CorpusShares had no other way for that MON to leave, and the test
run's 0.01 MON dividend is still locked in it.

reclaimDividend returns what is left of such a dividend to the issuer,
only after the record date and only when the supply at that date was
zero. A dividend with holders is theirs and it cannot touch it. Three new
tests; on chain, a dividend was declared on the new contract, the record
date passed, and it came back in full, leaving the contract empty.

CorpusShares alone is redeployed by DeployShares.s.sol at 0xAE1F…0fc7,
exact_match on Sourcify; apply-deploy overlays it from that script's
confirmed broadcast. The first one is listed as superseded with the reason.

/corpus-token's event list now says it is this server's writes, which it
is: the issuer can also write from scripts/shares.mjs, and those are in
the figures above but not in that log.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Stop showing numbers nobody measured, and 404 what does not exist
body:
The first browser pass against the Monad deployment found pages stating
figures that were not readings:

- /operator reported "0 protocol calls, 0 reverted" whenever the index or
  the ledger failed, because a failure was stored as an empty list. It now
  says "—" and why, and "no runs" means only that.
- /post showed "Your balance 0.0000 MON" with no wallet connected, and
  projected the whole escrow as "scoring shortfall" from a mean score of
  zero when no run had been scored. Its gas note named "the six tasks
  here" after a seventh was posted; it now says what the receipts show.
- /task said a task "was posted with createTask" when it was posted with
  createTaskUntil and a zero deadline; it now says what the state shows.
- /handheld said the arm reaches 408 mm beside a spec sheet saying 512.
  Both are true of different things, so it now names the solver's reach
  and reads it from REACH_MAX.
- The manifest answered matches: false for a task with nothing committed,
  which reads as a mismatch. It is null until there is something to compare.

Pages that call Monadscan's index no longer ask when this deployment has
no key: next.config.ts exposes whether one exists, not the key, so an
unconfigured index is a stated reason rather than a 503 and a console
error on every load. A failure that does happen shows the server's own
sentence instead of "would not answer just now".

/station/999, /station/abc, /licence/<unminted>, /operator/nope were 200s
saying "not found"; they are 404s, asked of the contract the same way
/task asks, and still rendered when the chain does not answer.

/lab refetched its list once on the receipt, and on Monad the endpoint
serving the read can be a block behind the one that confirmed it, so the
list omitted the task the line above had just announced. It asks again
each second until the task is there. The Privy policy name is shortened
to Privy's 50-character limit, and the changelog is regenerated from this
repository's own history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Deploy Thenar to Monad testnet
body:
Twelve contracts from DeployMonad.s.sol in one broadcast, seventeen
transactions, every receipt status 1, AxonProtocolV2 at block 64987386.
Five tasks seeded at 0.002 MON a run, six slots each, task 4 with a
seven-day deadline. The verifier is 0xC7D1…893D on the protocol and the
manifest; the corpus issuer 0x9a6A…e6b2 owns CorpusShares and SalesLog.
All twelve are exact_match on Sourcify for chain 10143.

apply-deploy.mjs now reads the newest record whose every transaction has a
successful receipt, not run-latest.json: forge wrote a second record a
minute after the broadcast, simulated against an endpoint that had not
caught up, with nonces five behind, addresses that belong to other
contracts and no receipts at all, and it overwrote run-latest with it.
Addresses are written checksummed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Write the Monad test plan, and answer an unconfigured snapshot with 503
body:
docs/TESTPLAN-MONAD.md lists every page, route, contract, integration and
flow with the exact result that counts as a pass, against the live Monad
deployment through a real browser.

The first sweep found /api/snapshot answering 502 when no bucket is
configured. 502 says an upstream failed, and here there is no upstream:
the drill already answered 503 for the same missing bucket. The snapshot
now answers 503 for no bucket and 502 only when a bucket refuses the
upload, and the OpenAPI document says both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Script the demo take for the Monad build
body:
Every beat is confirmed from a Monad receipt with status 1 rather than a
mirror node or another chain's explorer: the lab's 0.004 MON bounty, the
policy's refusal, an agent's one-cent USDC pull with its SalesLog entry
read back through servedCount, and a dividend declared in CorpusShares.
The share beat is the dividend, not a run's issued shares, because a take
cannot produce a Selfie-Checked human. The intro names Monad Metropolis,
Track 4, and the pronunciations learn Monadscan and MON.

Nothing is recorded or voiced yet; tts.py has to run again before
cut.mjs, since the beat ids and the narration changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Write the README and the Metropolis submission for the Monad build
body:
The README says what runs today and on which chain, what Monad does here
that another chain would not, and what is not proven. SUBMISSION.md makes
the case for Track 4 — identity, provenance, data ownership and agent
trust, each enforced by a contract — and says which commits existed
before Metropolis and which were written for it.

The Avalanche-era plans, audits and test reports move to docs/history,
where the Avalanche README already was. The Blitz audits keep their place
with a note that the project has come back to Monad on a new deployment.
.env.example names the keys the Monad build uses, and no contract
addresses, which live in lib/deployment.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Sell a task's corpus to agents over x402 in USDC on Monad, and log every sale on chain
body:
An agent asks /api/agent/corpus for one task's file and is answered 402
with two offers. One is x402's exact scheme on eip155:10143: a cent of
USDC as an EIP-3009 authorisation the agent signs, which the Monad
facilitator submits and pays the gas for. The other is AgentKit's: if
World's AgentBook maps the agent's wallet to a verified human, its first
three pulls are free, counted in the database so a restart does not hand
them out again. An agent with nobody behind it is not refused; it pays.

Settlement happens only after the export succeeds, so a task with nothing
recorded answers 404 and charges nothing. Every pull that succeeds is
hashed as served and written to SalesLog with that sha256. The log keeps
each sale in storage as well as in an event, because on Monad an event
more than a hundred blocks old cannot be read back through a public RPC,
and servedCount(sha256) lets a buyer check its own copy against the chain.

/agents states the terms the 402 states and lists every pull with its
settlement and its log entry. scripts/agent-buy.mjs is the buyer: it pays
from a wallet with USDC and no MON, hashes what it received and asks
SalesLog, not this server, whether those bytes were sold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Gate paid runs on a World ID Selfie Check, and make the humans who pass it the corpus' only owners
body:
A paid run needs a live human behind the address. The station asks for a
Selfie Check before the run rather than after it, the proof and the
wallet's own signature have to agree, and a nullifier binds one person to
one address. It is asked on any chain, because it is a signature and a
phone scan, and a wallet that cannot add Monad must still reach it.

A proof that passes puts the address on CorpusShares' control list, and
every settled run issues its driver's shares, scaled by the signed score
and named by the run's hash. The contract refuses a share for anyone not
on the list, so a bot farm can record runs and cannot own the corpus.
On Monad both writes settle in under a second, so the station reports the
run's shares in the same panel as its payout instead of promising them.

/corpus-token reads the shares from the contract: supply, holders,
dividends, and whether it would accept a share for a given address, asked
by simulation. scripts/shares.mjs is the issuer's side: the register, the
compliance check, a dividend in MON with a record date two minutes out,
and one holder's entitlement.

The issuer key is not the verifier's. The verifier signs scores and lives
only in the signer service; minting shares is a different authority.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Sign operators in with Privy, and give labs a budget Privy can only spend on bounties
body:
An email address is enough to be paid: Privy makes an embedded wallet on
Monad, and an operator who already has a wallet can still bring it. When an
embedded wallet exists it is the active one, because some extensions sign
transactions but refuse to sign the plain message the Selfie Check asks for.

A lab's budget sits in a Privy server wallet under a policy with one allowed
action: a transaction to AxonProtocolV2 on chain 10143 carrying at most
0.1 MON. /lab posts a bounty from it and then asks the same wallet to send
0.01 MON somewhere else, so the refusal is something a lab can watch
happen. Privy signs; Monad's RPC broadcasts, with a gas limit of the
estimate plus a tenth, because Monad charges the limit.

scripts/privy-lab.mjs creates the policy and the wallet once, tops the
wallet up from the deployer, posts a bounty and prints the refusal.

This also brings in the dependencies the next commits use: Privy, World
IDKit and AgentKit, and x402 with its EVM scheme.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Move Thenar back to Monad, and read its history from storage
body:
Every page settles on Monad testnet again, chain 10143, where Thenar was
built at Blitz. MON is the bounty, the payout and the gas. The Foundation's
RPC is first, with Ankr and thirdweb behind it, each probed for batched
calls before being listed; drpc is left out because it refuses the gas a
Multicall3 read asks for.

Monad's public endpoints answer eth_getLogs only a hundred blocks wide,
under a minute of chain. The feed, the standings, the observed gas cost
and the mean score all read the log from the deployment block, so on
Monad every one of them would have been empty. They read the contract's
own arrays through Multicall3 instead, a hundred runs per call, each read
once because the array only grows, and a run's transaction is the one log
in the block the run recorded.

Per-address history comes from Monadscan through Etherscan's V2 API. It
needs ETHERSCAN_API_KEY, and without one the pages say that instead of
showing an empty history.

The registry reads its addresses from lib/deployment.ts, lists only the
contracts that have one, and names what each leans on Monad for: the
sharded slot counter for parallel execution, the P-256 precompile, and a
sales log kept in storage because events alone could not be read back.
The Avalanche L1 page and the Warp attestation go: neither exists here.

The QA and end-to-end scripts talk to the same chain through
scripts/monad.mjs, and scripts/monad-run.mjs records a scripted, paid run
with a gas limit of the estimate plus a tenth, because Monad charges the
limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Put every contract on Monad in one broadcast, and give each run and task its block
body:
DeployMonad.s.sol deploys the whole set to Monad testnet in one go:
AxonProtocolV2, the passkey registry, certificates, the contribution
record, corpus access and manifest, referrals, the foundry, the prize pool
and confidential payouts, with five seeded tasks. The bounties are small
and set by REWARD_WEI, because Monad charges the gas limit and a deploy
estimated at 130% pays for the 30%.

Two contracts are new. CorpusShares is the corpus as shares: only an
address on its control list can hold, send or receive one, shares are
issued per run with the run's hash, and a dividend in MON pays whoever
held at a record date that has to be in the future when it is declared.
SalesLog records every corpus sale with the sha256 of the bytes served.
Both belong to a corpus issuer key, not the verifier.

A Trajectory now records the block it settled in and a Task the block it
was posted in. Monad's public endpoints answer eth_getLogs a hundred
blocks wide, so the app reads history from storage and finds a run's
transaction with a one-block query at the block the contract kept.

lib/deployment.ts is where the addresses live, written by
scripts/apply-deploy.mjs from forge's broadcast record, so no address is
ever typed in. scripts/monad.mjs gives every script the same chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Build the product on Avalanche Fuji
body:
Squashed from the 253 commits that took Thenar from Monad to Avalanche
Fuji and built the product there (8a90d40..2e1ac4d in thenar-io): the
station, the lab, the hub, policies, licences, referrals, the prize pool,
AxonProtocolV2 with escrow refunds and relayed passkey runs, the unit and
end-to-end suites, and the design system.

The Monad Blitz build is the history before this commit. What comes after
it is the move back to Monad.

subject: Point the repo at thenar.io and drop claims that no longer hold
body:
Every Railway URL in the docs, robots.txt and the scripts becomes the custom
domain. The one in vercel.json stays: it is the API proxy target, and the API
owns a SQLite file on a persistent volume that a serverless host cannot keep.

Also removes two things the README promised and the build no longer has: the
/passkey page, cut in 6111428 when wallet connect moved to RainbowKit, and
scripts/passkey-onchain.mjs, which does not exist. The precompile work is real
and stays documented against the fork tests that exercise it. Route count
corrected to ten, and the submission details are now a table at the top.

subject: README: correct the AxonProtocol test count
body: forge test reports 23, not 19; the suite grew with the sharding tests.

subject: README: inline demo GIF and a contracts section
body:
The video tag is stripped for some viewers, so the GIF carries the demo
inline and the release link carries the full cut. Adds the deployed
addresses, what each entry point does, and where the tests are.

subject: Embed the demo video in the README
body:
Recorded against the deployed build after the mirroring fix, so the payload
and the goal ring sit on the same side of the table as the arm reaching for
them. Both transactions in the cut are real and linked from the README.

subject: Un-mirror the payload, goal ring and trail
body:
The arm model is rotated -90 degrees about X, which maps its own plane-Y
onto three's -Z. The payload, the goal ring and the tool trail were all
placed from a plane-Y with the sign left positive, so every one of them
rendered mirrored across the table from the arm that was supposed to be
reaching for them.

The arithmetic was never wrong — the inverse kinematics land on the target
to the millimetre, which is why the grasp and the score worked while the
picture showed the block sitting on the opposite side, apparently untouched
and jumping about. Only the rendering carried the wrong sign.

subject: Fix space: auto-repeat was flipping the jaws back open
body:
Space toggled the jaws on every keydown, and a held key auto-repeats. One
press plus nine repeats — about half a second — flipped them open, shut,
open, shut and left them at 42 mm. Closing the jaws genuinely did nothing,
anywhere on the table, however close to the payload you were.

The toggle now ignores repeats, so one press is one change of state.

Space also activates whatever button has focus, and after Begin run that is
the End run button, so a press meant for the jaws could end the run instead.
Focus is dropped when a run starts.

subject: Stop the hero payload teleporting, and make the station payload graspable
body:
The hero attached the payload on the jaw opening alone, so the moment the
jaws closed the block snapped to the gripper from wherever it happened to
be, and at 76 percent of the cycle its resting place flipped from the pick
spot to the place spot in a single frame. Between those two it read as an
object floating around the table rather than one being carried.

It now rides the same keyframes as the arm — seated at the origin until the
grasp, carried until the release, seated at the destination after — and the
cycle alternates direction, so the loop never has to teleport it back to the
start.

The station's capture volume also reaches high enough that one press of Q
from the rest pose puts the jaws on the payload, and the readout says which
of the two things is wrong: how far away it is, or that you are over it and
too high.

subject: Make the payload actually graspable
body:
The capture test was a sphere measured to the payload's waist. The tool
cannot descend below 12 mm above the table and the waist sits at 37.5 mm,
so 25 mm of unavoidable vertical error came straight off a 55 mm budget and
left under 49 mm in the plane — and nothing on screen said whether you were
inside it, so finding it was guesswork. In practice the payload could not be
picked up.

The test is now a cylinder: within 90 mm in the table plane, and anywhere
along the payload's own height. The readout carries the distance to the
payload and turns to IN RANGE — PRESS SPACE once closing the jaws will
actually take it.

subject: Frame the hero arm from its real extent
body:
The camera sat about 1.08 m from an arm three quarters of a metre tall at a
32 degree field of view, so the hero was a close crop of the elbow — the
pick-and-place cycle it exists to show was off screen.

The distance is now solved from the arm's actual extent against the panel's
aspect, taking whichever of the two axes is tighter, so it frames the whole
cycle on a wide desktop panel and on a narrow phone one alike. Only the
distance is derived; the three-quarter view the product is drawn from is
unchanged.

subject: GSAP landing motion, step icons, canonical sitemap
body:
One authored sequence rather than scattered effects: the dimension rules
draw out from their centres, the headline settles, and the live chain
readings arrive last, because on a bench the measurement is the last thing
to appear. The run sequence reveals once as a batch on scroll.

Everything uses gsap.from, so the resting state is the visible one and
nothing is hidden if the script never runs, and the whole thing is skipped
under prefers-reduced-motion.

The four steps now carry drawn icons from the existing set, and the sitemap
points at thenar.io instead of the Railway backend, which would otherwise
have indexed every page twice.

subject: Revert the speculative viewport sizing changes
body:
Chased a blank station viewport that turned out to be the automation tab
being backgrounded: requestAnimationFrame is paused in a hidden tab, so
react-three-fiber never initialised its renderer and nothing mounted. The
canvas is fine in a visible tab.

viewport.tsx goes back to the version that was verified working, keeping
only the model path rename.

subject: Measure the station viewport off the settled layout
body:
The viewport is code-split and mounts under a grid row whose height is only
settled once the rest of the page has laid out. react-use-measure took its
first reading before that and fell back to 300x150, and because the row's
size never changed afterwards the observer had no reason to fire again.

Measuring undebounced off offsetWidth/Height reads the settled box, and one
dispatched resize on the frame after the GL context exists covers the case
where even that is early. RainbowKit's stylesheet also moved ahead of
globals.css in the layout, so its resets can no longer outrank Tailwind.

subject: Pin wagmi to 2.16.9 so the RainbowKit modal actually opens
body:
RainbowKit 2.2.11 declares wagmi ^2.9.0 as a peer and the project was on
wagmi 3.7.6. Nothing threw — useConnectModal simply handed back an
undefined opener and the connect button was a no-op, which the optional call
in useSession swallowed silently.

2.16.9 is the version that satisfies RainbowKit's baseAccount import without
dragging in the optional @x402 packages that 2.19 resolves statically and
Turbopack cannot find. Verified against the running app: the modal opens on
a real click, lists Browser Wallet and Coinbase Wallet, and closes again.

subject: Fix the settled migration order
body:
The index on the new column sat in the create block, which runs before the
ALTER that adds it. On any database that predated the column the index threw,
the whole exec aborted, and the migration below it was never reached — the
live backend answered every read with 'no such column: settled'.

The index now runs after the migration, where the column exists either way.
Verified against a database built without the column: it migrates and the
unverified legacy row is correctly excluded.

subject: Only show runs the chain actually accepted
body:
/api/submitted took any well-formed transaction hash on trust and wrote it
to the ledger. A reverted transaction has a valid hash too, so a batch of
replayed submissions that the contract correctly refused were recorded as if
they had settled — task #9 showed twenty submissions against four filled
slots, five of them the same score.

The receipt is now read back and has to say success, against this contract,
before anything is written, and a new settled column gates every read so an
unverified row can never reach a page. /api/reconcile holds the existing
rows to the same standard; it only reads the chain, so it can confirm or
retract but never invent, and running it twice changes nothing.

subject: Fix the deploy env, the footer wordmark and the stale control copy
body:
Three separate misses.

The Vercel env vars were empty strings — 'printf value | vercel env add' does
not pipe a value through, so both were created blank and every chain figure
on the deployed site read 0 while the same build read 11/9/3 locally. They
are public values, so they now live in vercel.json where they are version
controlled and inlined at build time rather than set by hand.

The footer wordmark is uppercase AXON, which the \bAxon\b rename never
matched.

The landing still told operators to use the arrow keys and E/D after the
station moved to drag plus WASD and E/Q.

subject: Prove money movement on chain, and record the locked-escrow finding
body:
scripts/money.mjs measures balances either side of every step against the
live contract: escrow funded, each run paid, policy minted, licence bought,
every contributor's share checked to the wei.

Two things it turned up. The payout is reward x score / 10000, not the whole
slot — a run is worth what it scored. And because of that, a completed task
keeps whatever the runs did not earn, with no refund, sweep or reclaim
function anywhere in the contract, so that remainder is locked permanently.
Fixing it means a new contract, which would orphan the policies and cap
tables now on chain, so it is recorded rather than done.

subject: Fix: the rebrand broke every signature; guard the domain on chain
body:
The rename swept lib/server/verifier.ts and changed the EIP-712 domain from
Axon to Thenar. The deployed contract hardcodes keccak256("Axon"), so every
submitTrajectory started reverting with BadSignature — the whole submission
flow was dead in production and /api/health still reported ok, because it
only compared the verifier address, never the domain.

The domain is restored and moved behind runDomain(), which now carries the
warning that it is not the product name. /api/health computes the domain
separator and compares it against the contract's own domainSeparator(),
which is added to the shipped ABI, so this class of break is caught by the
health check instead of by a reverted transaction.

subject: Deploy the frontend to Vercel at thenar.io
body:
The pre-existing thenar project was set to framework Other with output
public/, so it served static files and 404'd every route. vercel.json pins
the framework instead of relying on detection against those settings.

.vercelignore keeps the deployer and verifier keys, the contracts, the CAD
kernel and the database off the upload entirely — the verifier key belongs
to the Railway backend and nothing else needs it.

subject: Proxy /api to the backend origin when one is configured
body:
The API routes own a SQLite file on a persistent volume, which a serverless
host cannot keep. Splitting the deployment means the frontend has to reach
the backend's routes rather than its own copies of them.

beforeFiles, not afterFiles: the default phase only runs when nothing on the
filesystem matched, and the route files exist in both deployments, so the
local copies would answer and the proxy would never fire.

subject: Remove passkeys, move wallet connect to RainbowKit
body:
The passkey surface is gone: the page, its ABI, the registry address and the
script. The deployed PasskeyRegistry and the contract's ABI entries stay as
they are, because both are real and already on chain.

Wallet connect is RainbowKit, themed onto the product's palette rather than
left on the default purple. WalletConnect-backed wallets only appear when a
project id is configured, so the modal never offers a wallet that cannot
pair. hasWallet is gone with the branches it guarded — the modal handles
discovery and install links itself.

subject: Station: pointer drag and WASD; seed a fanned-out cap table
body:
The 3D viewport ignored both the mouse and WASD, so the first two things
anyone tries in a robot teleop view did nothing. Dragging now moves the tool
in the camera's ground plane, and WASD drives the same target as the arrows.
Raise/lower moves from E/D to E/Q so D can mean right.

Also adds the seed scripts that filled task #9 from four distinct operators
and minted its policy, so the foundry shows a cap table that actually fans
out rather than a single 100% contributor.

subject: docs: second Monad audit after the v2 deploy
body:
The first audit's honest verdict was that this used only Monad's EVM-compatible
half and could run on any fast EVM chain. Three of the four capabilities it
named as missed have since shipped — the P256 precompile, parallel-execution-safe
writes, and Multicall3 batching — so that verdict no longer holds and this
records why.

Fifty further features, ranked by how load-bearing Monad is to each. The two
capabilities still idle are the 150M gas limit and the 128 KB contract size,
and everything at the top of the list attacks them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: feat(contracts): v2 — sharded slot accounting and passkey-authorised runs
body:
AxonProtocol redeployed at 0x89384f46e430F37DB61Afb98810eba995C0d6Ed4,
verified exact_match, seeded with eight funded tasks.

Sharded slot accounting closes the contention bug this project's own audit had
been carrying. A single slotsFilled counter is one storage slot every operator
on a task writes to, which on an optimistically parallel chain forces them to
re-execute serially. Each operator now writes only the shard their address maps
to, each shard carries its own quota so the common path needs no cross-shard
read, and a caller whose shard is spent falls back to a scan — the only path
that can contend, and only at the margin.

Writing it surfaced a real flaw first: address-based sharding confines an
operator to one shard, so a four-slot quota could block the five-run allowance
the product promises. The tests caught it; the shard floor now sits above the
per-account cap.

submitTrajectoryWithPasskey lets an operator authorise a run with a secp256r1
signature over the trajectory instead of their wallet, composing with the
already-deployed PasskeyRegistry rather than duplicating the precompile call.
The verifier still signs the score, so an operator still cannot mint their own.

Also fixes a README bug that had been in the repo since the deployment table
was written: it contained literal {axon} and {verifier} placeholders from an
f-string that never interpolated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: docs: describe what the project actually ships, and prove the passkey path on chain
body:
The docs had drifted badly. README, PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and TESTPLAN.md
contained no mention of the passkey work at all, README still claimed six
routes when there are eleven, and MONAD.md called the P256 precompile 'verified
working, entirely unused' — which stopped being true when it shipped.

MONAD.md now marks that miss closed and updates its verdict: the audit was
written when this could have run on any fast EVM chain, and the precompile
makes that no longer so. The two remaining misses, the staking precompile and
EIP-7702, are still named as open, as is the parallel-execution contention bug,
which needs a redeploy that would orphan the trajectories already recorded.

scripts/passkey-onchain.mjs closes the last verification gap: register() and
authorise() had never executed on chain, only the view path. Both now have,
with replay and forgery refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: docs: give every one of the 100 ideas its own disposition
body:

subject: feat: ghost trail, reach envelope, context recovery, clipboard, keyboard help
body:
The ghost trail draws the path the payload actually travelled, which is the
exact line the smoothness term scores — the difference between 'you lost 40%
on smoothness' and seeing why.

The reach envelope appears only when the operator hits the limit, which was
previously a text readout with nothing to point at.

A lost WebGL context left a black rectangle and no error anyone could see; it
is now caught and explained, and nothing recorded is affected.

Hashes and addresses are copyable, the submit flow announces itself to a
screen reader, a fast double click can no longer send two transactions, and
the station's controls are on ? because it is a keyboard-driven surface.

Plus robots.txt, a sitemap and a web manifest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: feat(passkey): verify secp256r1 signatures through Monad's P256 precompile
body:
PasskeyRegistry is deployed at 0xD6dE823EE979c4aAD3ba8eDe05f6E363DE65E165 and
verified on the explorer. It binds a secp256r1 public key to an address and
checks signatures against EIP-7951's precompile at 0x0100 — the same curve and
encoding a passkey uses, and something Ethereum mainnet cannot do at all.

Ten tests run against a fork of Monad testnet rather than a local chain,
because the precompile is the whole point and etching over a precompile
address is not permitted. The vector is a genuine WebCrypto signature. The
check costs about 16k gas.

/passkey proves it live: the browser generates a real key, signs a message, the
chain accepts the signature and refuses the same one with a bit flipped.

This is the answer to the product's actual bottleneck — operators are gig
workers and the seed phrase is where that funnel dies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(chain): batch reads through Multicall3 instead of one call per trajectory
body:
The leaderboard oscillated between one and two operators and between fourteen
and fifteen runs while the chain held twenty-three trajectories and two
contributors. Each poll issued one eth_call per trajectory, the public RPC caps
at fifteen requests a second, and the failures were quietly dropped by a
filter — so every poll under-reported by a different amount.

Monad testnet carries Multicall3 at the canonical address, so declaring it on
the chain collapses a whole screen of reads into a single call.

A partial read is also no longer treated as a smaller answer: if any read in a
batch fails the hook throws, and the surface shows its error state rather than
quietly rendering an incomplete ledger.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(station): an unreadable task no longer flickers between error and spinner
body:
useTask polled every six seconds, so a task id that is out of range — which
reverts every single time — bounced between 'Could not read that task' and
'Reading task #999 from the chain…' indefinitely. A check landing inside the
retry window saw an empty page.

Polling now stops once a read has errored, and the error state wins over the
retry spinner on both the station and the task page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(station): remount the rig per run so the payload actually resets
body:
The previous attempt passed a runId into the scene and reset the refs in an
effect. It never fired: children of <Canvas> live in a separate
react-three-fiber reconciler root, and a prop change on the parent does not
reliably re-run their effects. Measured directly in the browser — after Run
again, the tool stayed at the exact coordinates the previous run ended on and
the deviation never left 9.8 mm, so a second run began already inside the goal.

The rig is now keyed on runId, so a new run remounts the scene. The GLB is
cached by useGLTF, so nothing reloads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(station): the payload did not reset between runs
body:
The scene reset keyed on `start`, a module-level constant, so it ran once on
mount and never again. A second run began with the payload still wherever the
previous run had left it — including inside the goal, which returned IN
TOLERANCE for a run where the operator never touched the arm.

The station now bumps a runId on every run and the viewport resets its payload,
arm pose, gripper and held keys when it changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(api): a missing taskId no longer exports task 0
body:
Number(null) is 0, so GET /api/dataset with no parameter silently answered for
task 0 instead of rejecting the request. It now returns 400, and a non-numeric
value says what it received.

Also links the transaction in scripts/claim.mjs, which was the one submission
path that reached the chain without recording its hash — the feed and the
dataset export reported that run as never submitted when it had settled.

Adds scripts/audit-links.mjs, which holds the store and the chain to each
other: every recorded transaction must exist and have succeeded, and every
unlinked run must genuinely have no record on chain. It caught a run that was
on chain but unlinked, and it exits non-zero on any discrepancy.

subject: fix(post): form validity gates the button, not the wallet
body:
A task with a three-character instruction or zero slots showed its inline
error but left the button live, because the disabled check only applied once
a wallet was connected. The definition of a task is wrong or right on its own;

The two gates are now separate, and the button says which one is failing:

subject: test: prove the deferred-payment path on chain
body:
A contributor whose wallet refuses transfers must not be able to revert their
own submission, so the protocol credits claimable instead of pushing. That
branch was covered by a unit test but had never executed against the real
chain.

RefusingContributor deploys, submits, refuses the payout, and then claims it:
the submission succeeded, 0 MON landed, 0.005958 MON was credited, and claim()
pulled exactly that once it stopped refusing.

All five contract entry points are now proven on Monad testnet — createTask,
submitTrajectory, mintPolicy, licensePolicy and claim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: feat(deploy): live on Railway with a persistent trajectory store
body:
https://web-production-2d1d0.up.railway.app

All five health checks pass in production and the end-to-end proof runs green
against the deployed app, not just localhost — a real transaction settled in

The trajectory store sits on a mounted volume, so runs survive a redeploy.

subject: test: exercise the whole task lifecycle on chain
body:
createTask -> fill every slot -> mintPolicy -> licensePolicy, asserting the
cap table sums to 100% and that a licence pays the contributor exactly its
share plus, here, the protocol fee, since this deployment's treasury is the
same address.

Two Monad behaviours cost real debugging time and are now handled explicitly:

- The reserve check is far stricter than value + gas. The same licence call
  reverted with "Signer had insufficient balance" at 0.3 MON and settled at 2.
- Consensus and execution are pipelined, so a receipt means a transaction was
  ordered, not that its state change has landed. A freshly funded account still
  failed the next transaction until the script waited for the balance to
  actually appear.

On chain now: 15 tasks, 18 trajectories, 7 policies minted, 2 licences sold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(station): the run measured itself before the operator had moved
body:
The settle detector was true from the first frame: the payload starts at rest
and ungrasped, so 700 ms into every run it measured the payload at its starting
position and returned OUT OF TOLERANCE / 0.00. Driving the arm correctly made
no difference — the verdict was already in. The headless end-to-end test never
caught it because it constructs samples directly and never touches the UI.

A run can now only be measured once the payload has actually been picked up and
let go, and an operator who cannot finish has an End run escape instead of
being stuck.

Also recalibrates the smoothness term. The jerk reference was 3.0, taken from a
synthetic path; real runs driven through the station measure 25.9 m/s^3 when
driven carefully and 51.3 when snatched, so the term scored zero for everybody
and a quarter of the score was dead weight. The band is now 18..60 from those
measurements, and check-loop asserts both endpoints stay inside it.

The score breakdown now shows the raw measurement beside each percentage —
deviation in mm, jerk in m/s^3, elapsed against par — which is the product's
own rule and what made the miscalibration visible in the first place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: docs: Monad integration audit, contract changes, and 50 ranked features
body:
Verified against the live chain rather than the docs: sub-second blocks, a
150M block gas limit, and the P256 precompile at 0x0100 confirmed working with
a real WebCrypto secp256r1 signature (tampered signatures refused).

The honest finding: Monad is genuinely the settlement layer here, but only its
EVM-compatible half. Nothing yet needs Monad specifically, and the contract
contains a parallel-execution contention bug — every submitter writes one
shared slotsFilled slot, which is the exact anti-pattern on an optimistically
parallel chain.

subject: feat(brand): orange on black, new type stack, and the Axon mark
body:
The category's incumbent runs Borna + formularMono + Press Start 2P on acid
green over black. Borna and formularMono are commercial, so the closest free
equivalents carry the same feel — Hanken Grotesk for display and body, DM Mono
for every measured value — and Press Start 2P, which is free, stays as the
pixel voice on the wordmark. The neutral steps are the same greys; the accent
is ours.

Colour still means data: signal orange carries value and live state, the
verdict pair sits deliberately off that hue so a reject can never read as a
payout, and controls stay achromatic.

The arm's collars are regenerated in the signal colour from cad/arm.py, so the
geometry and the interface agree rather than the 3D being dressed separately.
The reduced-motion hold pose is now mid-traverse, which is the arm's most
legible frame instead of whichever one the clock started on.

New mark: an A drawn as two arm links rising to a pivot, crossed by the datum
line where a measurement would be taken.
